children: , the chipmaking giant fighting to rebuild its manufacturing edge, crossed the one-million-wafer milestone using high-numerical-aperture extreme-ultraviolet technology Tuesday. Shares surged approximately 7.6% to $103.07, creating roughly $37 billion in market value as investors rewarded tangible progress inside Intel's foundry operation.

The company and ASML also proved that reticle stitching can pair High-NA equipment with existing six-inch masks, potentially sparing chip designers from an expensive redesign. Intel said certain Intel 18A layers manufactured with High-NA delivered performance matching or beating equivalent layers made with conventional EUV systems. The technology has already moved beyond the laboratory and into limited Panther Lake production.

Intel's latest quarter produced $16.1 billion in revenue alongside approximately $8.4 billion of negative adjusted free cash flow. The stock rally is a loud vote of confidence, but the valuation is louder: GuruFocus places GF Value at $31.96, leaving the $103.07 share price 222.5% above that estimate. High-NA strengthens Intel's manufacturing story; profitable outside foundry contracts must now justify the premium.

title: Intel's 8% Jump Adds $39 Billion as High-NA Hits One Million Wafers
